conceptBreakdown.content: The stem is the ascending axis of the plant body developing from the embryonic plumule. It is positively phototropic, negatively geotropic, and differentiated into nodes (points of leaf attachment) and internodes (regions between adjacent nodes).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.1 Underground Stem Modifications (Perennation Organs)
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.1 Underground Stem Modifications (Perennation Organs)
conceptBreakdown.content:
Underground stems store food, allow vegetative propagation, and act as organs of **perennation** to survive unfavorable seasonal conditions:

1. **Rhizome**: Dorsiventral or upright, prostrate, thick horizontal stem growing parallel beneath soil surface. Possesses distinct nodes, internodes, brown scaly leaves, axillary buds, and adventitious roots (*Zingiber officinale* - Ginger, *Curcuma longa* - Turmeric, *Canna*).
2. **Stem Tuber**: Swollen tip of an underground specialized branch. Lacks adventitious roots. Possesses "eyes" (nodes containing axillary buds protected by scale leaf scars) (*Solanum tuberosum* - Potato).
3. **Corm**: Short, stout, vertically growing, unbranched condensed underground stem with distinct circular nodes. Larger than a bulb (*Amorphophallus titanum* - Zaminkand, *Colocasia*, *Crocus sativus* - Saffron).
4. **Bulb**: Highly reduced, disc-like underground stem surrounded by dense concentric layers of fleshy scale leaves storing water and carbohydrates (*Allium cepa* - Onion [tunicated bulb], *Allium sativum* - Garlic).

conceptBreakdown.title: 2.2 Sub-Aerial & Aerial Stem Modifications

      PHYLLOCLADE (*Opuntia* / *Euphorbia*)       CLADODE (*Asparagus* / *Ruscus*)
      ├── Unlimited growth (multiple nodes)     ├── Limited growth (1 or 2 internodes)
      ├── Entire stem modified into leaf-like   ├── Lateral branch modified into leaf-like
      │   green photosynthetic organ            │   structure
      └── True leaves reduced to spines         └── True leaves reduced to scales
conceptBreakdown.content:
### 1. Sub-Aerial Vegetative Spreaders
• **Runner**: Slender, prostrate creeping branch with long internodes that roots at nodes (*Cynodon dactylon* - Lawn grass, *Oxalis*).
• **Stolon**: Slender lateral branch arising from stem base that grows arching upward before touching soil to form a new plant (*Fragaria* - Strawberry, *Morus*).
• **Offset**: Short, thick, rigid lateral branch with brief internodes bearing a rosette of leaves above and a tuft of adventitious roots below (*Eichhornia crassipes* - "Terror of Bengal", *Pistia*).
• **Sucker**: Slender lateral branch originating from the underground stem portion that grows obliquely upward through soil to produce leafy shoots (*Chrysanthemum*, *Banana*, *Pineapple*).

### 2. Aerial Stem Transformations
• **Thorns**: Hard, straight, woody, pointed modified axillary buds used for defense against herbivores (*Citrus*, *Bougainvillea*). *(Prickles are superficial cortical outgrowths lacking vascular bundles, e.g., Rose; Spines are modified leaf structures, e.g., Opuntia)*.
• **Stem Tendrils**: Slender, spirally coiled, sensitive structures derived from axillary or terminal buds that wrap around supports (*Passiflora*, *Cucurbits* - Cucumber, Pumpkin, Watermelon, *Vitis* - Grapevine).
